title: An Invoices import file with the old column names imports like a new one
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create two import files for this test from the downloaded Invoices import template, each with one Labor row for an existing customer, *Line Title "Replace tie rod" and Line Description "excessive play": file A keeps the template's headers, with a new invoice number, invoice A; file B is the same, with its two headers renamed to "*Line Title - What are you doing" and "Line Description - Why are you doing it", with another new invoice number, invoice B.
  • Give invoices A and B numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Start on Settings, then Invoices under Data Import in the Settings left menu.
custom_steps:
1. Upload file A.
  2. Upload file B.
  3. Click Work Orders in the top bar.
  4. Click the All tab.
  5. Switch the list to List view.
  6. Pick Imported in the Status filter.
  7. Type the shared start of the two invoice numbers in the Search box.
  8. Click invoice A.
  9. Go back to the list.
  10. Click invoice B.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • "All invoices have been imported successfully." shows.

Step 2:

  • "All invoices have been imported successfully." shows.
  • No message says a column is missing or should be removed.

Step 3:

  • The Work Orders page opens.

Step 4:

  • The All tab is shown.

Step 5:

  • The work orders show as a list.

Step 6:

  • Only imported work orders are listed.

Step 7:

  • Invoices A and B are listed.

Step 8:

  • Invoice A opens; its line reads "Replace tie rod" as the title and "excessive play" as the description.

Step 9:

  • The list is back, with invoices A and B.

Step 10:

  • Invoice B opens; its line reads "Replace tie rod" as the title and "excessive play" as the description, exactly like invoice A.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 15 (14 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10133 (Story 4, The Imports)

  • S4-R3: “The importer accepts the old column names as well as the new ones. A file carrying either spelling validates and imports identically. Column names are matched regardless of capital letters and surrounding spaces, as every column already is.”
  • S4-R5: “The old name is accepted as the column it became: it is neither reported missing nor reported as a column to remove.”
  • Key Decisions: “Renaming an import column never breaks an existing file. The importer validates headers strictly, so a plain rename would have failed every spreadsheet a shop has saved. It now maps the old header onto the new one before it validates. A file may even mix the two spellings.”

From: Jira tickets and comments under epic SV-11257, and bug SV-11850 (saved in sources/jira-2026-10-27/ALL-TICKETS-2026-10-27.md), read 27 Oct 2026

  • SV-10133, Nemanja Djuric, 8 Oct 2026 (Ready for QA testing): “Import a file using the old headers ("*Line Title - What are you doing", "Line Description - Why are you doing it"): it imports the same way, with no missing-column error.”
  • SV-10133, Nemanja Djuric, 21 Oct 2026: “Work Orders → All tab → Status → Imported. Selecting Imported clears the other statuses and only works in List view (in other views it's greyed out: "Imported work orders open in List."). Then search by invoice number or customer name; partial text works, so "QA10133" finds all four.”

Not yet checked against a build by us: the QA build (sv10130.qa.shopview.com, QuickBooks host qb1.qa.shopview.com) and staging carry this change, and this case has not been run on either.
